Commentary.Commentary: Do New Zealand have the momentum? Do they have the belief? From one angle, if you look at it, if the home side gets somewhere around 450-500, it could be a difficult task for the Proteas second time around. On the other hand, if the tourists can take a leaf out of the Kiwi bowling book this morning, they can put New Zealand under pressure. Stay tuned...

South Africa will be disappointed but they will know that if they can bowl well, they can still stay in the game. Cutters and change of pace will be effective and perhaps Maharaj might need a spin partner or two. The worrying aspect from the batting point of view would be that only 3 out of the top 6 got into double figures.

Mission accomplished as far as the Kiwi bowling is concerned. The aim would have been to not let the Proteas get away this morning and they allowed the visitors only 79 runs, picking up 6 wickets. Wagner got the important wicket of Elgar while Boult picked up 3 this morning, finishing with 4 overall. Jeetan Patel did his best in troubling the batsmen and picked up 2 scalps too.

The home side will know that it can take its foot off the pedal at its own peril. Numbers 9, 10 and 11 can bat for the Proteas and another 50 runs would be very vital. Join us back at 1340 local (0040 GMT) for all the action post Lunch.

Fine bowling display from the Kiwis. Neil Wagner bowled his heart out this morning, delivering 11 overs on the trot and was well assisted by Boult who got a couple of wickets today. Jeetan Patel bowled much better as compared to yesterday and the pressure has been constantly put.

Elgar and Bavuma started cautiously this morning before Wagner got rid of the centurion. The Proteas then lost their way as they slipped from 252/4 to 298/8. They now have Philander and Rabada at the crease and will hope to get as many as they can.
Excellent session for New Zealand. 72 runs in 28 overs with 4 wickets. Their aim was to stifle the run rate and when they achieved that, wickets came in clusters.

RUN OUT CHANCE MISSED! Oh dear... Watling... Rabada pushes it towards point and sets off for a single. Trent Boult gets to the ball and fires a good throw to Watling. Philander is slow and seems to be short. Watling collects and looks to whip the bails off but for some reason he stops, then misses the stumps when he tries! He is embarrassed as the players walk off the field. Not a great Test match for him as far as keeping is concerned. LUNCH ON DAY 2!

It was an attritional day of Test cricket as South Africa wrestled the advantage after electing to bat. Dean Elgar has led the charge with a fine century. He got good support from skipper du Plessis and has found an able partner in Bavuma. Can the Kiwis break this partnership and keep the Proteas under 350? Or is a huge first innings total on the cards? Hello and a warm welcome to the second day of the opening Test between New Zealand and South Africa in Dunedin.
... DAY 2, SESSION 1 ...

The pitch seems to have eased out after the moisture has dried up and batting looks to be easier. South Africa still have got some batting left and will be aiming somewhere close to 350-375. The Kiwis, on the other hand, will aim to break this partnership quickly tomorrow morning and then go through the lower middle order. Join us at 1100 local (2200 GMT, previous night) to check how Day 2 unfolds. Until then, you can catch all the action from the SL-Ban Test and the Afg-Ire T20I. Adios! Take Care!

The Kiwis will feel let down by their own efforts. They had a tremendous opening session but then a simple dropped catch of Elgar on 36 changed the tempo. Since then, they have been on the receiving end. Apart from Neesham, no one has gone for runs but wickets is what you need more in Tests.

The Kiwis started well, nipping out 3 quick wickets but after that it was slow progress. The 126-run stand between du Plessis and Elgar stalled them and in spite of Faf's wicket, they could not quite get through the middle order. Elgar has held forte with a brilliant unbeaten 128 while Bavuma has shown good patience.

South Africa's day. Elgar's day. What an outstanding knock. He has scored more than half the team runs and held one end up. The strike rate was not that great but it hardly matters on Day 1 of a Test match.

Goes forward to this floated delivery outside off, Bavuma pushes it away with his front pad.
Bowls this outside off, Bavuma leans forward to defend but misses the ball and it hits his pad. The impact was outside off.
Tosses this one around off, Elgar looks to drive it down the ground but it takes the outside edge and goes towards point. The slip fielder chases it and cuts it off.  Three runs taken!
Length ball, fifth stump line, Bavuma shoulders his arms.
Bowls this on a length outside off, Bavuma leaves it alone.
FOUR! Short of a length delivery, outside off, Bavuma cuts it elegantly through point for a boundary. Brilliant shot that!
Bangs this one short again, the southpaw gets under it and pulls it towards the diving mid-wicket fielder. Single taken!
Bouncer and well directed, Elgar moves back and ball goes past him to the keeper. Dharmasena says one bouncer for the over.
Short delivery and down the leg side, Elgar has no reason to play at it.
Floats this one outside off, Bavuma places it towards the off side.
Tosses this one around off, Bavuma kneels and sweeps it through fine leg. Two runs added to the total!
Short and turning in, Elgar nudges it to fine leg for a single.
Sprays this down the leg side, Elgar works it around to mid-wicket.
Fuller and on the sticks, Elgar comes forward and drives it towards the bowler.
Bowls it slower through the air, and outside off, Elgar shoulders his arms.
Marginally ahead of length outside off, Bavuma lets it through to the keeper.
Short of a length delivery, which comes back in, Bavuma gets on his toes to punch it to the cover fielder.
Length ball, swinging back in, Bavuma strides forward and drives it towards covers.
Fullish delivery, around off, Bavuma comes forward and defends it towards the off side.
Angles this one on a length around off, stands in his crease and blocks it.
Bangs this short  around rib height, Elgar hops and nudges it towards square leg. One run added to the total!
Neil Wagner is back on. He will bowl from around the wicket. Short balls can be expected!
Drags his length back and bowls it outside off, Bavuma punches it towards covers.
Loops this one around middle, Bavuma flicks it towards backward square leg.
Bowls this one outside off, looks to defend but the ball goes past his outside edge.
Tossed up, turning in, Bavuma works it around towards mid-wicket.
Floated around off, Bavuma leans forward and dead-bats it.
Tosses this one outside off, Bavuma leaves it alone.
Jeetan Patel is back into the attack!
Outside off, left alone.
Full and outside off, driven towards mid on for a single.
FOUR! That is a terrific shot. Short of a length outside off, Bavuma gets on top of the bounce and punches it behind point for a boundary!
Outside off, left alone.
Short and outside off, punched off the back foot through the covers for a run.
Full and around off, swinging in, Bavuma is early into his flick and the ball goes off the inside half of the bat through square leg. A single taken.
Full on middle, swinging in, worked wide of mid on. The ball stops near the fence and three runs are taken.
Top edge, safe! FOUR! A short ball outside off, Bavuma looks to pull but is hurried into it. Neil Wagner fives it a good chase from deep fine leg but cannot get to the ball.
FOUR! Full and wide outside off, Bavuma leans and drives it through point for a boundary.
Full on middle, swinging in, flicked straight to short mid-wicket.
WIDE. That is short and too high, Bavuma ducks and the square leg umpire signals to the main umpire that it is a wide.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Landed outside off, watchfully defended.
7th Test ton for Dean Elgar, second against New Zealand!

FOUR! Century for Elgar! Wonderful innings. He has held South Africa from one end. Had a few nervous moments early on but has come off those superbly. A short ball outside off, Elgar pulls it through mid-wicket for a boundary! His arms go up in the air, the helmet comes off and the entire South African team applauds from the dressing room. Well played.
Another bouncer, closer to the batsman, Dean ducks again.
A good bouncer outside off, Elgar sways away.
Fuller and wider outside off, DE goes after this one and gets it past cover. Returns for the second and moves to 98. The stand moves into double figures.
Full and just outside off, Dean defends watchfully.
On a good length outside off, Elgar gets across and shoulders arms.
Comes over the wicket for the final ball, bowls a tempter outside off, fuller in length but Bavuma does not attempt the drive. Watches it go past.
Fuller and closer to the off stump, this time TB puts bat to ball and pushes it towards over.
Comes in a long way from outside off, Temba shoulders arms again.
On a good length outside off, defended towards cover.
Landed on a fuller length again, outside off, this one bounces after pitching but after it passes Bavuma who does not flirt with it.
Full and outside off, left alone.
TRENT BOULT to continue from the other end.
FOUR! Full and wide outside off. Elgar reaches out and flays it behind point. A hit away from the century now.
Driven towards the mid on region.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.
Defends it from his crease.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
Outside off, left alone.

Welcome back for the final session. 28 overs left in the day. The first session belonged to New Zealand while the second went to the Proteas. Who will win the day? The players are back onto the field.
... DAY 1, SESSION 3 ...

The pitch is looking flatter now and batting has become considerably easier. The Kiwis had to toil hard in the afternoon session but they will hope to get into the lower middle order quickly now, given that Faf is gone. Elgar has played beautifully for his 92 and will aim to anchor the innings. Join us back at 1600 local (0300 GMT).

Things could have been different had Bradley Watling hung on to the catch offered by Elgar down the leg side. After that, he started dealing in boundaries, along with his skipper as the duo threaded a 126-run stand for the 4th wicket. However, just when it seemed like the Kiwis cannot buy another wicket, Faf sold it to them, losing his cool minutes before Tea.
Excellent session for South Africa. 90/1 in 31 overs. Would have been even better had du Plessis not got out before the break but the visitors are in control of the game.
Another wide ball outside off, fuller in length, Bavuma lets it pass. TEA ON DAY 1!
Full and wide outside off, not played at.
Comes around the wicket now...
Full on middle, worked straight to widish mid on.
Landed outside off, angling away, left alone.
Similar ball, pushed wide of mid on for a quick single.
Full and around off, pushed towards mid on.
TRENT BOULT to bowl the final over before Tea.
Outside off, left alone.
Action replay of the previous delivery.
Similar ball, defended with a dead bat towards point.
On a good length around off, defended to the leg side.
Outside off, left alone.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

FOUR! Up and over! Flighted outside off, Elgar comes down the track and lofts it over mid off for a boundary! 150 UP FOR SOUTH AFRICA and that takes Elgar into the 90s. Can he get to his century before the break?
Full and outside off once more, worked towards mid on once more.
Similar line, worked wide of short mid-wicket towards mid on.
Landed around middle, defended towards short leg.
Full and outside off, Elgar lunges and defends.
TEMBA BAVUMA walks in at number 6, replacing his skipper, with less than 10 minutes to go for Tea.

OUT! CAUGHT! Neesham eventually gets his man. A short ball outside off, du Plessis swivels and pulls it away. Normally, he hits these out of the park but there are two odds here. A. The ball is well outside off, which means he has to fetch it and put more power. B. It is the longest part of the ground. As a result, the pull shot is aerial but does not have the power. Trent Boult settles under it at the square leg fence. Du Plessis stands there, looking at his bat and then trudges off. End of another fine knock and the 126-run stand is broken. That should lift the Kiwi spirits.
Outside off, left alone.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.

NOT OUT! Inside edge saves Faf. On a good length outside off, nips back in a long way, Faf gets across and hops to defend but misses and is hit on the pads. Neesham appealed, umpire Dharmasena thought long and hard and then nodded his head, raising his finger. Du Plessis straightaway went up for the review after signalling to his partner that it was too high. But technology shows a deviation on the Snickometer as the ball passes the bat. The third umpire overturns the decision giving the reason as an inside edge. Not quite sure whether Faf thought there was any wood involved.
Faf du Plessis has been adjudged LBW! He has taken the review though...
Full and outside off, du Plessis drives it towards mid on.
Landed outside off, blocked with an angled bat-face towards gully.
Landed outside off, Dean lets it go past.
Full and outside off, Elgar leans and pushes it towards mid off.
Driven towards the mid on region.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman. They pick up a single.
10th Test Fifty for Faf du Plessis, first against New Zealand!

FOUR! AMAZING! He has been looking to do that for long. Comes down the track, gets to the pitch of the ball and drives it effortlessly through the covers. Finds the gap and the boundary. That is some way to getting to your half century. Well played.
Full and on middle, driven towards mid on.
Landed outside off, left alone.

EDGED, FOUR! That is unlucky for Neesham. He makes the ball angle into the left-hander and forces Elgar to play. Then he induces an outside edge which goes into the slip cordon but in the gap between second slip and gully. Races away top the third man fence. The stand moves to 121 now.
FOUR! Too loose a ball. Short and outside off, Elgar just places it through point and beats the fielder's dive to his right. Into the fence. Moves to 83 with his 16th boundary!
Closer to the batsman and the stumps, Dean gets across and defends.

FOUR! Well played. A short ball outside off, angled in, extra bounce, Elgar rides it nicely and opens the face of the bat accurately to guide it between gully and backward point for a boundary. The stand is worth 113 now.
Full and wide outside off, a gentle loosener, left alone.
JIMMY NEESHAM finally gets a bowl. One slip and a gully in place.
A touch shorter around off, punched towards point.
A little bit slower utside off, loopy as well, driven towards short extra cover again.
Thrown up outside off, driven straight to short extra cover.
Comes down the track and pushes it back to the bowler.
Fuller on off, du Plessis gets down and gently paddles it over the keeper towards fine leg for a couple.
Full on middle, Elgar works it wide of mid on for a quick single.
Driven towards the mid on region. Good over for South Africa - 14 from it.
FOUR! A bit streaky. Full and wide outside off, du Plessis looks to drive but gets a thick outside edge which goes between point and gully to third man.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot for a single.
100-run stand is up! Terrific fightback.

FOUR! SWEET! Similar length, fuller outside off, but the line is a bit wider. Elgar comes forward and drives it wide of mid off. The fielder races to his right and dives but the ball goes through! This has been a really good partnership putting them into ascendancy. Elgar moves to 73 and this is his 14th boundary.

FOUR! Not quite well timed but he will get a boundary. Fuller in length, around middle, Elgar looks to drive but is a tad early into the shot. The ball goes off the inner half of the bat, wide of mid on and reaches the fence.
On a good length around off, du Plessis punches this wide of mid off. Kane Williamson gets across to his left and slides to stop the ball. Keeps the batsmen to just a single.
Full and around middle, pushed back to Santner.

QUICK SINGLE. Full and around off, FdP hits this inside out wide of mid off. Kane Williamson quickly gets to the ball and has a shy at the bowler's end but misses. Faf was in though. Perhaps it was a last minute decision from the skipper to run. Moves to 40.
Full and straight, chipped straight to short mid-wicket.
Advances again and flicks it towards mid-wicket. He is not afraid to come down the track frequently, is Faf.
Comes down the track, Santner sees that and drags his length down a fraction. Faf has to adjust and pushes it towards cover.
The arm ball around off, du Plessis defends from his crease.
Full and straight, defended watchfully from the crease.
Full and outside off, pushed straight to wide mid off.
Full but down the leg side, du Plessis falls over but manages to flick it through square leg for a run. That swung a bit late.
Another short ball, pulled towards deep mid-wicket for a single. The stand is worth 90 now.
Full and outside off, driven straight to mid off.
Starts the over with a bouncer, Elgar ducks.
The arm ball but down the leg side, du Plessis whips it straight to square leg.
This is around off, extra bounce, FdP is surprised but manages to keep it down.
Into the pads, very straight defended towards short mid-wicket.
Very full, around off, du Plessis makes room to hit it inside out but finds short extra cover.
The arm ball, around off, coming in, Faf gets his bat down in a hurry to defend.
Full and around middle, defended watchfully.
Fuller outside off, Elgar is not sucked into the drive and shoulders arms.
Another bouncer, a sharper one, DE ducks again.
A bouncer around middle, Dean ducks.
Full an straight now, pushed towards mid on.
Full and outside off, pushed straight to cover.

FOUR! Terrific shot. Fractionally short in length outside off, Elgar picks it up in a trice and pulls it through square leg for a boundary. replays show that umpire Bruce Oxenford at square leg is busy making some notes. Lucky guy. The ball just flew past him and he was not even watching.
The batsman gets to the pitch of the ball and defends it.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Full and outside off, FdP comes down the track and drives it towards cover.

OVERTHROWS. Full on middle, Faf works it straight to Neil Wagner at square leg. The fast bowler picks up the ball and returns a wild throw, right at du Plessis' head who ducks. There is no one backing up and by the time deep point gets across, two runs are taken.

Massive LBW shout, not given, no review taken. The arm ball, around middle, du Plessis looks to flick but misses and is hit on the back pad. Santner wants a review but Williamson does not grant him his wish. It might have been angling down the leg side.
Full and outside off, Faf comes down the track and drives it wide of mid off for a quick run.
On middle and leg, tucked wide of mid-wicket for a single. Moves to 60.
Outside off, left alone.
Outside off, punched towards cover.
The batsman works it down the leg side.
Landed on middle and leg, Elgar looks to tuck it away but misses and is hit on the thigh pads.
NEIL WAGNER is back on.
Full and outside off, driven straight back.
On middle and leg, worked towards square leg.
The batsman dances down the track and does well to block the ball.
Full and outside off, watchfully blocked.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.
DRINKS BREAK.
Landed outside off, spinning away, watchfully left alone.
Outside off, pushed towards cover.
Full on middle, pushed back to the bowler.
FOUR! SUBLIME! Full and outside off, Elgar leans and drives it through the covers gloriously. Mitchell Santner gives it a chase but in vain. 100 UP FOR SOUTH AFRICA. The stand is worth 81.
Around off, defended towards point.
Full and outside off, pushed to the off side.
Comes down the track and pushes it back to the bowler.
Very full around off, pushed towards mid off.
Slower in pace, defended to the leg side.
Outside off, punched towards cover.
Around off and middle, worked towards deep mid-wicket for a single.

Comes down the track, Santner shortens the length and Elgar is forced to push it towards point. The fielder throws it towards Watling who is not watching and the ball goes through. Short leg backing up dives to his right but misses. Elgar wants a run off the overthrow but by that time, deep square leg comes in and du Plessis sends his partner back.
Full and just outside off, watchfully blocked.
Full and outside off, pushed towards mid on.
Landed outside off, Faf shoulders arms and the ball goes off his pads, then onto Watling's helmet towards the leg side.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.
Just outside off, du Plessis wrestles it towards short mid-wicket.
Landed around off, defended to the leg side.
Very well played. Pushes this with soft hands wide of mid off and gets a run.
Comes down the track again and works it towards widish mid on.
Full and outside off, Faf looks to drive but gets an inside edge back to the bowler.

MISFIELD, FOUR! Full on middle, du Plessis comes down the track and pushes it towards mid on. Trent Boult comes charging in to his left, aiming to pick up and throw but he misses it and the ball goes through to the fence.
The arm ball, arrowed in from off stump, du Plessis defends stoutly.
Full and around off, pushed straight to mid on.
Spinners from both ends now. MITCHELL SANTNER is back on.
Full on middle, flicked a bit uppishly towards short mid-wicket.
Goes back and works it through mid-wicket for a single. Moves to 30.
Turn and bounce. Around leg stump, du Plessis looks to flick but the ball spins past the bat, bounces and then goes off Bradley Watling's gloves towards leg slip.
A discussion between Williamson and Patel. Gully comes into place. Jeet Raval it is.
On the pads, worked past short leg towards square leg for a quick single. The stand moves to 70 from 141 balls.
Fuller outside off, Dean pushes it towards cover-point.
Landed outside off, Elgar comes forward and then watches it go.
The batsman has pushed it to the cover region.
Excellent yorker around off, dug out towards mid off.
Landed outside off, angling away, left alone.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman.
Full and outside off, du Plessis leans and drives it through the covers where the fielder makes a good diving stop.
Comes around the wicket and bangs it short outside off, angled in, punched towards short cover.
The batsman works it down the leg side. Two runs added to the total.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
A touch shorter around middle, Dean stays back and blocks.
Full and outside off, Elgar comes forward and defends.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Outside off, left alone.
Outside off, punched through the covers for a single.
Full and outside off, let through.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Landed outside off, defended back to the bowler.
Outside off, left alone.
6th Test Fifty for Dean Elgar, first against New Zealand.

FOUR! This outfield is becoming lightning quick now. A length ball on the pads, Elgar just helps it towards the square leg fence. Brings up a very gritty half century, a knock which started with a struggle but has become composed as and how the innings has progressed.
TRENT BOULT changes ends.
Landed outside off, Faf shoulders arms.

EDGED, FOUR! Full and outside off, du Plessis looks to drive but this is a quicker delivery, the slider and the ball goes off the outside edge, well wide of slip to the third man fence! The stand moves to 62 from 119 balls.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot.
Landed outside off, turned wristily towards short leg.
Landed around off, du Plessis defends it towards point.
Full on off, flicked towards short mid-wicket.
JEETAN PATEL is back on.
Full on middle, pushed towards mid on.
Fuller on middle, pushed towards mid on.
Landed outside off, Elgar gets across and shoulders arms.
Gets it past short leg this time for a single.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.
Shorter in length, flicked towards square leg but short leg intercepts.
Around middle and off, defended solidly to the bowler.
The batsman has pushed it to the cover region.
FOUR! PRISTINE! Full and outside off, Elgar leans and drives it wide of extra cover for a boundary!
Full and around off, blocked back to the bowler.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

Excellent running. Full and outside off, du Plessis pushes it towards mid off. Trent Boult slips in his followthrough and suddenly Faf calls for the single. Takes everyone by surprise, includig his partner. Elgar sets off late and in the meanwhile, Neil Wagner comes charging in from mid off to his left. However, the single is completed with ease.
Driven towards the mid on region. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Full and just outside off, watchfully defended.
Fuller on middle, pushed through mid on for a single. The fielder is a bit deep.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
50-run stand comes up in 97 balls!
Shorter around middle and off, du Plessis goes back and works it through mid-wicket. The ball stops near the ropes but by then, the batsmen take three. Excellent rearguard action by these two.
Landed outside off, punched towards point.
This is slightly fuller, outside off, a touch wide, DE shoulders arms.
A bouncer outside off, Dean ducks.
Landed outside off, punched towards point.
Nips back in from outside off, Elgar defends it to the leg side.
Full and outside off, pushed towards mid off.
Landed outside off, pushed towards point.
Full and around off, flicked wide of mid-wicket for a run.
Full and just outside off, pushed back to the bowler.
Advances down the track, pushes this towards Neil Wagner at mid on, takes him on, induces pressure and Wagner fumbles. A single taken.
Fuller a touch, driven wide of mid off.
Full and just outside off, du Plessis blocks it out.
Landed outside off, DE lets it through.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
FOUR! Half volley down the leg side, Elgar flicks it to the fine leg fence. Moves to 40 with his eighth boundary.
Landed outside off, Dean comes forward and pushes it towards point.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.
DROPPED! Simple catch. Full and down the leg side, Elgar looks to tickle it fine. There is a noise as the ball passes the bat and Boult starts to celebrate but then Watling fluffs a simple chance.
TRENT BOULT to bowl from the other end.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.
EDGED, LUCKY! Full and around off, Faf lunges to defend but gets a thick inside edge onto his pads. The ball flies past short leg who is late to react.
Landed around off, pushed towards cover.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Landed outside off, punched towards short extra cover.
Welcome back for the second session. The players are out in the middle. MITCHELL SANTNER will start off proceedings to Faf du Plessis. Here we go...
... DAY 1, SESSION 2 ...
The second session should be slightly easier for the batsmen. New Zealand would love to have a look-in at the lower middle order of the Proteas though. Join us back at 1340 local (0040 GMT).

Trent Boult set it up nicely getting the wicket of Cook and then Patel applied the choke on the batsmen. Runs were hardly coming and eventually that led to wickets, a couple of them, with Wagner getting Amla and Duminy in the space of 5 balls. Elgar has looked better as the innings has progressed while du Plessis continues to impress.

New Zealand's morning, without a doubt. They picked up 3 wickets and conceded just 63 runs, in 31 overs. Faf du Plessis and Dean Elgar have taken things under control a bit but the first 75 minutes went at a snail's pace for the Proteas.
Landed outside off, Elgar opens the face of the bat and guides it towards third man but gully intercepts with a dive to his right. LUNCH ON DAY 1!
A man goes out for the hook for Elgar.
Landed outside off, punched towards cover. The fielder gets across from point and slides to his left, fumbles but no run is conceded. There is a man at cover backing up.
On a good length around off, pushed towards short mid-wicket.
A bouncer down the leg side, Elgar ducks.
Slightly fuller, pushed towards cover this time.
This could be the last over before Lunch...
On a good length around off, defended to the off side.
On middle and leg, tucked behind square leg for a single.
EXTRA BOUNCE. Down the leg side, Dean comes forward to defend but the ball goes past the inside edge and hits him high on the back thigh.
Full and straight, watchfully blocked.
Looped up a bit, outside off, Elgar lunges and pushes it toward cover.
On middle and leg, flicked towards mid-wicket.
Full on middle, pushed towards mid on.
MITCHELL SANTNER comes on to bowl now, giving Patel a break.
On a good length again, punched through the covers where a diving stop is made.
On a good length around off, Faf goes deep in his crease and blocks.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
FOUR! Nice timing. Full and outside off, du Plessis leans and drives it through the covers for a boundary. the stand is worth 40 from 56 balls.
Full and outside off, angling away, left alone.
Full and outside off, pushed towards point.
Full on middle, pushed towards short mid-wicket.
Landed outside off, dabbed towards cover.
Full and just outside off, pushed towards cover.
FOUR! Full and down the leg side, Elgar just tickles it through square leg for consecutive boundaries!

EDGED, FOUR! Short and outside off, Elgar rocks back to cut but there is extra bounce which induces an outside edge. It goes into the gap through, behind point and races to the fence. Elgar moves to 31 with his 6th boundary. The stand is worth 32 from 49 balls.
On a good length around off, blocked back to the bowler.
Full on middle, pushed through mid on where Trent Boult makes a sliding stop.
Outside off, angling away, left alone.
Landed outside off, watchfully defended.
Full again, outside off, pushed towards third man but gully intercepts.
Full and outside off, swinging in, du Plessis looks to drive but gets a thick inside edge.
On middle and leg, clipped straight to square leg. 11 from the over, that gets the scoreboard moving a bit.
Full and just outside off, watchfully defended.
Full and around off, pushed towards deepish mid on for a single. 50 UP FOR SOUTH AFRICA. It has been a struggle.

FOUR! That is edgy. Landed outside off, du Plessis looks to push this through the covers but the ball goes off the outside edge, past slip and beats backward point to the third man fence. Faf moves to 13 from 16 balls.
FOUR! MURDERED! Full and outside off, du Plessis gets down and sweeps it powerfully through square leg for a boundary! The stand moves to 23 from 38 balls.
Full and outside off, du Plessis comes forward and opens the face of his bat to gently guide it past slip towards third man for a couple.
Very full outside off, driven straight to widish mid off.
This one is at the stumps and DE defends.
FOUR! Nicely done. On a good length outside off, Elgar opens the face of his bat and guides it through the slip cordon, between third slip and gully and gets a boundary.
Keeps it full outside off, angles it in, but pretty wide enough for Dean to play. Lets it through.
Comes back in a long way, Elgar defends watchfully.
Full and outside off, blocked to the off side.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Full and just outside off. flicked towards mid-wicket once more.
Nips back in from outside off, Faf looks to defend but gets a thick inside edge onto his pads.
Outside off, worked towards short mid-wicket.
Full and outside off, defended to the off side.
Outside off, left alone.
A bouncer to end he over, from middle to leg, DE ducks.
Full and just around off, pushed back past the bowler, but straight onto the stumps at the other end.
Full and outside off, pushed towards mid off.
Full and straight, coming back in, Dean pushes it towards cover.

FOUR! Elgar is growing in confidence here. Full on the pads, Elgar flicks it through mid-wicket. The ball stops near the ropes but makes it in the end. Elgar moves to 23 with his 4th boundary. The stand is worth 13 from 20 balls.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Appeal for a caught behind! Landed outside off, Faf gets across to defend but is beaten. There is an appeal but umpire Bruce Oxenford calms him down.
Full and outside off, pushed towards short mid-wicket.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads for a single.
FOUR! Outstanding timing. Shorter and on middle, Elgar just works it through square leg and the outfield takes the ball to the boundary!
The batsman has pushed it to the cover region.

Oohh.... flighted outside off, Elgar comes down the track and looks to flick but is beaten in flight. The ball goes of the outside edge through backward point. Elgar comes halfway down the track for a single but Faf sends him back. There is a misfield but still no single is taken.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground. Spirited effort by the fielder to save runs for his team.
Full and outside off, eased through the covers. Kane Williamson gives it a good chase and slides near the boundary to save a run. Three taken.
A short ball outside off, pulled straight to short mid-wicket.
Full and outside off, driven straight to mid off.
Full and outside off, left alone.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.
Wide outside off stump, the batsman leaves it alone.
Brave leave! Full and outside off, coming in with the angle, Elgar lets it through and the ball does not miss the stumps by much!
The batsman has been beaten by the turn and flight on that one.
Full and outside off, driven straight to mid off.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.
FAF DU PLESSIS walks in at number 5, replacing Duminy.

OUT! There is glove! Wagner gets his second in five balls! A short ball around off, an absolute brute, Duminy is caught by surprise and tries to sway away. He is not able to totally avoid it though and the ball goes off something to Ross Taylor at first slip. Umpire Dharmasena rules it out on the appeal but Duminy takes the review. Replays show the ball hitting the grill of the helmet but a closer inspection on Hot Spot shows that the ball brushes the gloves, then the helmet. Duminy has to go! What an over from Wagner.
Has Wagner got two in the over? Duminy has been given out caught behind. He has reviewed it though.
Works this wide of mid on for a quick run.
Full and straight, pushed back to the bowler.
Full and outside off, pushed towards point for a single.
JP DUMINY walks in at number 4, replacing Amla.

OUT! BOWLED! Wagner strikes on return! Full and around off, Amla looks to drive but the front foot does not move at all. That creates a big gap between bat and pad and the ball swings back in, goes right through the gate and hits the middle and off stumps.
Full and outside off, squeezed towards point.
NEIL WAGNER is back on.
FOUR BYES! Down the leg side, Elgar lets it through and poor Watling is blinded. Not able to get around in time. Patel apologizes.
Full and around off, pushed towards cover.
Full and around leg stump, watchfully defended.
The ball is way wide on the leg side but the batsman still goes after it.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Played to the mid-wicket region by the batsman.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Wide outside off, left alone.
Outside off, watchfully defended.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads.
The ball is way outside the off stump, easy leave for the batsman.
Outside off, played straight to point.
DRINKS BREAK.
Full and around off, watchfully defended. End of a riveting opening hour.
Outside off, a touch wide, left alone.
Around middle and off, Elgar goes too hard at it, pushing the ball back and his bottom hand comes off the bat.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.
Amla is underway. Similar ball to the previous one, this time Amla juts flicks this with soft hands through square leg and takes a single off his 20th ball.
Landed outside off, worked straight to short mid-wicket.
Full and around middle and leg, swinging away, pushed towards mid off.
Landed outside off, left alone.
FOUR! PRISTINE! Full and straight, Elgar drives this down the ground, beating mid on. Moves into double figures. That will give him some confidence.
On a good length around middle and leg, worked towards short mid-wicket.
Wide of the crease, bowls it too straight, flicked straight to short mid-wicket.
Whoa! Full and outside off, Elgar looks to defend but the ball swings away to beat the outside edge.
Beautifully bowled. Tosses this outside off, Hashim looks to defend, playing for a little bit of turn but the ball goes straight on with the arm and beats the outside edge.
Full and straight, flicked towards mid-wicket once more.
Landed outside off, watchfully defended.
A bit too straighter, whipped straight to mid-wicket again.
Full and outside off, flicked straight to mid-wicket.
Landed around off, worked towards square leg.
Outside off, pushed straight to point. That is a terrific over of Test match bowling.
Comes from wide of the crease, angles this into the left-hander from a short of a length, Dean looks to defend but does so awkwardly.
Keeps this full, outside off, Elgar shoulders arms.
On a good length around middle, DE stays back to defend but the ball stays low and hits the toe end of the bat.
Beauty. Bowls it full, closer to the off stump, forces Dean to play at it and then makes it go away, squaring him away. Beats the outside edge.
Full and outside off, swinging away, left alone.
Full and outside off, Amla blocks patiently.
Landed outside off, a bit of bounce, worked towards short leg.
Slightly on the pads, flicked straight to mid-wicket.
Landed outside off, watchfully defended.
Full and around off, flicked straight to short mid-wicket.
Full and outside off, worked wide of mid on for a single.
Slips this down the leg side, HA misses his flick.
Hmmm.... this is closer to the off stump, on a good length, Hashim shoulders arms again but the ball straightens a bit and threatens to hit the stumps. Misses the off pole in the end.
Similar ball, angling away from outside off, Amla lets it through again.
Shorter in length, outside off, steep bounce, HA shoulders arms.
Full and straight, more swing, Hashim plays it with soft hands, very late, towards short mid-wicket.

EDGED, DOES NOT CARRY! Beautiful bowling. Full and around off, swinging in, Amla pushes at it and gets a healthy outside edge. However, luckily for him, it does not carry to the diving Jimmy Neesham at third slip.
Landed outside off, well blocked out.
The batsman has played it towards mid-wicket.
Full and outside off, watchfully blocked out.
Slightly shorter, worked towards short mid-wicket.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.
Full and around off, more swing for Boult, Amla defends.
HASHIM AMLA walks in at number 3, replacing Cook.

OUT! LBW! Boult has struck. That is a serious piece of  misjudgement. On a good length around off, Cook gets across and shoulders arms. But to his horror, the ball swings back in and hits him on his pads. Boult appeals, umpire Dharmasena thinks for a while and then raises his finger. Cook does not even bother reviewing and walks off shaking his head. Hawk Eye shows the ball to be clipping the top of the bails. So would have stayed out even if Cook had reviewed it. Good start for the Kiwis.
Banged in short around off, Elgar looks to pull but there is no real timing. The ball goes wide of short mid-wicket and the batsmen take a single.
Fuller and on the pads, flicked straight to short mid-wicket.
Better line, closer to the off stump, pushed towards cover.
On a good length wide outside off, left alone.
Fuller in length, around off, SC comes forward and flicks it towards mid-wicket.
One more. Patel lands it in the same area, Stephen clips it towards square leg.
Same ball once more, good consistency, worked towards square leg once again.
Shorter in length, worked towards square leg.
Similar ball, defended again.
Landed outside off, worked straight to short leg.
EDGED, SAFE! Full and outside off, Dean looks to drive but gets a thick outside edge. However, it does not carry to Tom Latham to gully.

That is a ripper. In the avenue of apprehension, just outside off, on a good length, Elgar is indecisive whether to play or leave, tries to play but the ball moves away. He is squared up and the ball whizzes past the outside edge.
Better line. Full and around off, coming in with the angle, DE blocks it watchfully.
Shorter in length, well outside off, left alone once more.
On a good length this time, outside off, Dean shoulders arms again.
Landed wide outside off, left alone.
Landed outside off, defended watchfully.
Outside off, full again, worked straight to short leg.
Full and around off, Cook looks to defend but gets squared up and the ball goes off the leading edge towards cover.

Oh dear... that is ugly. DE comes down the track a month early, has a hack, does not get to the pitch of the ball and it goes off the inside half, just wide of short leg towards square leg. A single taken.

LBW APPEAL! Turned down! No review taken. Patel lands this around off, slides it on with the angle and beats Dean's lame push. The ball hits him high on the thighs and that is probably why umpire Bruce Oxenford turned down the LBW appeal.
Nice flight, outside off, Elgar pushes it towards point. The length was a bit short.
Wow. Interesting. Spin is in. JEETAN PATEL to bowl.
On a good length but wide outside off, another leave.
This is outside off, does not swing and SC shoulders arms comfortably.
Much better ball. This is in line of the stumps, which means Stephen has to play. He does and prods at it. The ball swings back in a touch, takes the inside edge and hits him on the pads.
Holds the length back a touch, keeps the line closer to the off stump, angles the ball away, but Cook lets it go once more.

Neil Wagner seems to be bowling with a scrambled seam. That is okay if the ball is a bit older and you want reverse swing but with the new cherry you would want conventional swing. Tim Southee and Trent Boult present the seam in a much better fashion.
Fuller and wide outside off, left alone again.
On a fuller length outside off, allowed to go through.
Much better, full and around middle, watchfully defended.
FOUR! MARVELLOUS! Full and outside off, Elgar comes forward and drives this through mid off. The fielder is a bit wide and the ball races to the fence! First boundary of the match.
This is wider outside off, easy leave.
One more leave outside off.
Landed outside off, let through.
Outside off, played straight to point.
Similar ball, a touch shorter than the previous one, tucked through square leg for a single to get off the mark.
Full and straight, but does not swing. DE misses his flick and is hit on the pads. Boult appeals but the umpire shakes his head. Sliding down the leg side.
Slips this down the leg side, shorter in length, Dean lets it go.
Outside off, swinging away, left alone.
Lovely ball, full and swinging away, around off, Elgar gets slightly squared up but manages to push it to cover.
Elgar finally gets on strike...
Full and swinging, but down the leg side, clipped behind square leg for a single.
Bends his back, generates steep bounce from a short ball around leg, Stephen hops and gets across, nudging it towards square leg for a quick single.
On a good length outside off, angling away, Cook shoulders arms. That barely carries to the keeper.
Full and around off, swinging back in, defended towards cover.
This is wider outside off, shorter in length, let through.
Fuller and straighter, tucked straight to mid-wicket.
A wayward start. A short ball down the leg side, Cook lets it through.
NEIL WAGNER will share the new ball with Boult.
On middle and leg, nudged through backward square leg for a single to get this Test underway.
Fuller and wider outside off, let through.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman.
Outside off, left alone again.
Full and outside off, left alone.

The players are out in the middle. We are ready for some red-ball action. Stephen Cook and Dean Elgar are the openers for the Proteas. TRENT BOULT will start off proceedings. Cook to face. Here we go!

TEAM NEWS - The Proteas have gone in with more or less the same Test side, with Morne Morkel coming in the side. They have one spinner in Keshav Maharaj. The Kiwis, on the other hand, have gone in with two spinners in Mitchell Santner and Jeetan Patel. No Tim Southee.

TOSS - The spin of the coin has gone Faf du Plessis' way. SOUTH AFRICA CHOOSE TO BAT FIRST. A decision which seems to be dictated by the future conditions of the track. Many would have been tempted to bowl first. This is the first time a team has elected to bat in this country in a Test match since January 2011. Wow.
PITCH REPORT - There seems to be a lot of grass on the track which should support spin as the game goes on.
WEATHER - It is a stunning day. Not a cloud in the sky with the sun shining brightly.

After a close contest in the ODIs, we are down to the Tests between New Zealand and South Africa. Both teams have been on a good run of late, so this should be fun. Having said that, the Proteas will test the home side's resolve with both bat and ball. Hello and a warm welcome to the opening day of the first Test between New Zealand and South Africa in Dunedin.
